summary.description: Everyday English for someone who doesn't know the code. Shape: one short paragraph saying what the PR changes and why it matters (explain any technical term in a few plain words, e.g. 'saved in the browser (localStorage)'); then 'It also does a few other things:' and a short markdown bullet list, if there are other changes; then one or two sentences with the overall verdict, ending with the problems that need fixing as a numbered list (one plain sentence each), if there are any.

ticket_coverage.description: One item per acceptance criterion in the ticket, in ticket order. Empty if the ticket couldn't be loaded.

requirement.description: The criterion's number and a plain-words description, e.g. 'Requirement 1 (store login info securely on the server)'.

status.description: Two or three words, e.g. 'Done', 'Mostly done', 'Not done yet', 'Probably fine', 'Can't check here'.

note.description: One to three short everyday-English sentences: what shows it, or what is missing. Point at a finding by its number in the summary list when it is the reason.

path.description: Repo-relative path in the PR head.

line.description: Line number in the PR head version of the file (RIGHT side).

pre_existing.description: True when the problem existed before this PR and the PR only extends it.

title.description: A short plain-words headline, e.g. 'Users can stay logged in after the inactivity timeout'.

body.description: The comment as it will be posted, in everyday English: what is wrong, a concrete example of when it breaks, and how to fix it.

before_release.description: Everyday English: steps outside the code that must happen before release (deploys, settings, other teams). Empty string if none.
